text:
The response is largely accurate. The speed figures (142 to 156 lines/hour, about 10%), error rates (0.62% to 0.41%), the 17% gain for new staff, the 64% preference, the $210,000 cost and 14-month payback all match the source. The "levelled off within four weeks" wording is a fair paraphrase, and the limitation about a single company is included. It covers the points a manager needs: performance, accuracy, new-staff effect, staff views, cost, caveat and takeaway.

The main failure is the explicit length limit. The response runs to roughly 200 words, well over the 120-word cap, so it fails a direct instruction. Some of that length is padding, such as the opening sentence, the "worth keeping this limitation in mind" line and the repeated framing in the takeaway. A tighter version could have kept every key figure in under 120 words. Accuracy is high, content coverage is good, but concision is poor and the word limit is clearly breached.

Score: 4
